title: Fundamental limits on state preparation for an open qubit
authors: D. A. Abraamian, L. V. Lokutsievskiy, A. N. Pechen
abstract: We analytically determine the ultimate limits of state preparation in two-level open quantum systems driven by coherent control. For a dissipative qubit governed by a GKSL master equation, we give an exact characterization of the reachable set in the Bloch ball. Dissipation excludes a region of states in the Bloch ball which cannot be approached even under arbitrarily strong coherent driving, and we prove that this region has a nontrivial geometry whose boundary is a surface of revolution around the $x$-axis which is analytic except for two conical singularities. We derive a closed-form control protocol for moving on this boundary, and construct an explicit protocol that steers the system arbitrarily close to any prescribed boundary state. These results provide a complete geometric constructive description of reachable qubit states in the standard dissipative environment, establishing fundamental bounds on controllability and state-preparation fidelity for open two-level quantum systems.
summary: This paper analytically determines the precise boundaries governing what states can be prepared in an open qubit under coherent driving. It proves that this boundary forms a specific surface of revolution within the Bloch ball, detailing the geometric constraints imposed by dissipation. The results yield fundamental bounds on quantum control fidelity for such systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the ultimate geometric limits of state preparation (the reachable set) for an open qubit subjected to coherent external driving.
main_result: The boundary of the reachable set is proven to be a surface of revolution around the $r_x$-axis, which is analytic except for two conical singularities. A closed-form control protocol is derived to approach any state on this boundary asymptotically.
method: The analysis employs geometric control theory applied to the Bloch sphere representation of the qubit density matrix dynamics governed by a GKSL master equation.
model_or_system: The system is an open two-level quantum system (qubit) whose evolution is described by the GKSL master equation, incorporating free Hamiltonian ($\sigma_z$), interaction ($u\sigma_x$), and dissipation terms. The state space is analyzed in Bloch ball coordinates $(r_x, r_y, r_z)$.
key_observables: The reachable set $\mathcal{R}$ (or $ ar{R}$) within the Bloch ball; boundary points ($\partial\mathcal{R}$).
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\gamma$), coupling strengths ($\kappa$), and control field amplitudes ($u(t)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on asymptotic reachability, meaning boundary states are only approached in the limit of infinite time.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of the boundary $\partial\mathcal{R}$ as a surface of revolution around $r_x$, showing intersections with preparatory surfaces like the torus-like region $T$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by setting up the dynamics in Bloch coordinates, establishing that the reachable set is solid of revolution (Theorem 2), and then rigorously characterizing the boundary $\partial\mathcal{R}$ using separatrices and analytic curve descriptions (Theorem 3).
why_interesting: This work provides a complete geometric characterization of controllability for an open quantum system, which is fundamental knowledge for designing robust quantum control protocols in physical implementations like superconducting qubits or cavity QED systems.
